HA6a0f4edec4a9c7e0.content: Defendants 1 and 2 are barred from executing the decree or taking possession of the disputed land for one month following the payment of Rs. 8,000 to Defendant No. 3.

HA7f40313223e7ed57.content: Defendants 1 and 2 must execute a new Kabuliyat within one month of payment, accepting modified terms including a reduced commission rate of 2a. 6p. per ton.

HA6756ebae46b63e81.content: Defendant No. 3 must execute a new patta embodying a minimum royalty of Rs. 6,000 and a commission rate of 1a. 9p. per ton, replacing the original terms.

HA28f612aaaed01429.content: A decree reducing the amount payable by an agriculturist debtor without granting the same relief to non-agriculturist co-debtors is objectionable if it creates unequal treatment.
HA28f612aaaed01429.speaker: The Court

HAf8f09330216eff27.content: The decree should have explicitly directed that payment by co-defendants 2 to 7 would release only their interest in the mortgaged property from sale.
HAf8f09330216eff27.speaker: The Court

HAe56fe1b20ec64c14.content: The decree should have further directed that failure to pay by co-defendants 2 to 7 would result in the sale of the whole mortgaged property for the entire debt.
HAe56fe1b20ec64c14.speaker: The Court

HA0d9ab9976eb95722.content: Although the decree lacked clear directions, reading it as a whole and considering the actual decision reveals its plain implication regarding the split of debt and security.

Hef92cfe9cba8a3e1.similarities: Both cases involve execution objections where judgment-debtors claim separate property is immune from a decree obtained against an ancestor or prior party, relying on partition or statutory relief acts.
Hef92cfe9cba8a3e1.differences: The current case centers on Hindu law liability for pre-partition debt under CPC 53, whereas the historical case focuses on the Madras Agriculturists' Relief Act limiting execution against agriculturists' property despite a prior decree.
Hef92cfe9cba8a3e1.warrant: The historical case demonstrates that statutory relief acts can bar execution even against established decrees, suggesting that the current case's reliance on CPC 53 must be weighed against any potential statutory protections or specific compromise terms limiting the decree's scope.
